distinguishing_features: Uses a fixed micro-lamella array with micro-textured walls to pin nucleation to stationary high-shear sites, rather than pulsed recirculation of existing loop hardware
Decouples nucleation (stable site) from crystal growth (shear sweep) to continuously detach ice into slurry, rather than disrupting crud precipitation kinetics
Targets ice-solute interfacial detachment via shear-stress-vs-adhesion balance, not particle breakup/agglomeration of a solid crud phase
Adds a dedicated micro-channel heat exchanger with new pump rather than modulating an existing recirculation pump
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to continuously remove growing ice from the cooling surface so that a thin transient ice layer is maintained and solute is rejected into the bulk liquid, rather than allowing a thick insulating ice crust to trap solute.
parsed.viable_reason: The physics check is internally inconsistent and implausible: it claims Re>2000 turbulent flow in a 100 µm channel at 1 m/s (Re~100, laminar), uses laminar shear while citing turbulent friction, and asserts ice detachment at 5-15 Pa adhesion with a sub-10 µm layer that cannot be validated as written.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Pinning nucleation to fixed high-shear micro-textured sites and shearing off ice to decouple nucleation from growth is a genuine mechanistic departure not suggested by the pulsed-recirculation crud-disruption art.
